facts.statement: The RT-QuIC test, which was first created to find prion proteins, has been modified to identify alpha-synuclein seeds.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Adding the fluorescent dye thioflavin-T to the test allows researchers to watch the clumping process in real time and find very small amounts of misfolded protein.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: In diagnostic settings, the alpha-synuclein RT-QuIC test has a high rate of correctly identifying negative cases, ranging from 82% to 100%, and a variable rate of correctly identifying positive cases, ranging from 70% to 100%.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Newer versions of the test can be run on blood samples, which allows for a less invasive way to diagnose the condition.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Specific scores and kinetic measurements from the test can be used to evaluate how the disease is progressing and how well a treatment is working.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: A skin biopsy version of the test provides an alternative diagnostic option that is as accurate as methods using cerebrospinal fluid.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The study provides detailed step-by-step instructions for performing the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay.
facts.subject: other
